description: Permitting emotional, subjective note-taking (e.g., 'how bad it is') instead of objective descriptions.
risk: Reinforces anxiety and avoidance behaviors.

description: Waiting until end of day or later to record panic attack details.
risk: Accuracy and usefulness of documentation decrease, impeding effective intervention.

negative_action: Ignore patient resistance or anxiety about recordkeeping
description: Not addressing or minimizing the patient's discomfort with recordkeeping.
risk: Patient may avoid objective recording, hindering progress.

negative_action: Use vague generalities or retrospective recall
description: Substituting concrete, immediate documentation with general statements or delayed recall.
risk: Loss of essential detail undermines therapeutic value.

description: Presenting all anxiety as abnormal or harmful.
risk: Fosters unrealistic expectations and can stigmatize normal experiences.

description: Downplaying the patient's panic or distress.
risk: Can increase feelings of isolation or misunderstanding.

description: Supporting avoidance or escape as desirable solutions.
risk: Maintains anxiety and prevents corrective learning.

description: Teaching coping mechanisms before patient develops awareness of their symptoms and cycles.
risk: Patient may not understand or benefit from skills, and root problem may remain unaddressed.

description: Framing panic attacks as entirely random events without identifiable patterns.
risk: Reduces patient agency and obstructs skill development.

description: Suggesting interventions without scientific basis (e.g., pure positive thinking, generic meditation, vague advice).
risk: Can lead to ineffective treatment and deteriorate trust.

description: Normalizing without validating the patient’s true distress.
risk: Makes patient feel misunderstood and can damage therapeutic alliance.

negative_action: Provide inaccurate or oversimplified medical information
description: Giving misleading medical facts about panic symptoms.
risk: Could increase or create new fears and misconceptions.

description: Not validating or directly checking patient's understanding of concepts.
risk: Potential for untreated cognitive errors and misconceptions.

description: Supporting exaggerated or catastrophic explanations of symptoms.
risk: Amplifies anxiety and maladaptive beliefs.

description: Neglecting the influence of history or context on patient’s beliefs.
risk: Misses deeper underlying causes and reduces efficacy of therapy.

negative_action: Allow avoidance behaviors or safety signals to persist
description: Not examining or addressing avoidance or safety behaviors and signals.
risk: Prevents corrective learning and perpetuates anxiety cycles.

negative_action: Encourage use of safety signals/superstitious objects
description: Supporting reliance on safety signals or objects.
risk: Impedes mastery and maintains avoidance patterns.

negative_action: Rely on distraction techniques for exposure
description: Utilizing distractions instead of direct exposures.
risk: Reduces learning and maintains anxiety cycles.

description: Not explicitly listing all relevant safety behaviors.
risk: Unrecognized avoidance can hinder progress.

negative_action: Progress with exposures without baseline data
description: Starting exposures without adequate individual assessment.
risk: Exposures may be inappropriate and less effective.

description: Missing less obvious avoidance behaviors.
risk: Prevents full therapeutic engagement and change.

description: Treating hyperventilation or related symptoms as medically dangerous.
risk: Reinforces catastrophic beliefs and increases panic.

description: Promoting the belief that bigger breaths are better.
risk: Can worsen hyperventilation and anxiety symptoms.

description: Guiding overbreathing exercises with patients who have epilepsy, seizures, or cardiopulmonary diseases.
risk: Could cause serious medical complications.

negative_action: Introduce breathing skills in high-anxiety settings prematurely
description: Urging use of new or unfamiliar breathing methods in stressful contexts before skills are mastered.
risk: Could lead to skill failure and increased frustration or anxiety.

negative_action: Use breathing skills as safety behaviors
description: Employing breathing skills solely to avoid or escape anxiety.
risk: Impedes approach behavior and corrective learning.

negative_action: Criticize or provoke frustration during skill learning
description: Reacting negatively if patient struggles with skill acquisition.
risk: Reduces motivation and may increase resistance.

description: Suggesting that breathing issues or panic symptoms are life-threatening.
risk: Amplifies maladaptive beliefs and panic.

description: Not probing when patient reports unspecific fears.
risk: Impedes cognitive restructuring and clarity.

negative_action: Reinforce positive thinking or false reassurance
description: Offering reassurance not grounded in reality or evidence-based practice.
risk: Does not address underlying cognitive errors; may erode trust.

negative_action: Focus only on eliminating anxiety/physical symptoms
description: Neglecting cognitive change and overemphasizing symptom removal.
risk: Misses therapeutic goals and impedes recovery.

description: Suppressing or evading important subjects in therapy.
risk: Prevents emotional processing and corrective experiences.

description: Not attending to quickly arising negative cognitions.
risk: Leaves core cognitive errors untreated.

description: Portraying normal anxiety symptoms as harmful or risky.
risk: Reinforces fear and panic.

negative_action: Minimize required effort/time for skill mastery
description: Underestimating how much effort and time patients need to change.
risk: Can foster frustration and premature dropout.

negative_action: Confuse adaptive behaviors as loss of control
description: Framing adaptive coping during panic as failure.
risk: Reduces patient self-confidence and skill use.

description: Treating intense or repeated negative emotions as therapeutic failure.
risk: Undermines progress; promotes hopelessness.

negative_action: Conduct intense symptom induction without medical clearance
description: Doing high-intensity exposure exercises without ensuring medical safety.
risk: Patient may experience dangerous symptoms or medical events.

negative_action: Use coping skills as avoidance during exposure
description: Allowing coping skills during exposures instead of after.
risk: Reduces effectiveness of corrective learning.

description: Letting patients use avoidance, distractions, or safety objects/system during exposure tasks.
risk: Undermines learning and maintains anxiety.

description: Taking a judgmental stance toward patient effort.
risk: Reduces self-esteem and motivation.

negative_action: Focus on elimination of symptoms (zero anxiety)
description: Attempting to drive anxiety levels to absolute zero.
risk: Unrealistic goals may lead to disappointment and hinder learning.

negative_action: Discontinue exposures due to strong anxiety/symptoms
description: Stopping exposures solely because symptoms become intense (unless medically unsafe).
risk: Prevents effective learning and recovery.

negative_action: Use medication to block all anxiety/fear responses
description: Employing medication so symptoms are fully suppressed during learning periods.
risk: Obstructs acquisition of coping skills and mastery.

negative_action: Confuse one-off/forced exposure with systematic practice
description: Assuming brief or forced exposure is therapeutic rather than repeated, structured practice.
risk: May hinder long-term progress and reinforce avoidance.

negative_action: Allow continued use of safety behaviors/medications during exposures
description: Permitting distractions, safety signals, or fast-acting medications in exposure.
risk: Prevents corrective learning; reinforces avoidance.

negative_action: Treat absence of anxiety during exposure as success
description: Assuming complete lack of anxiety is desired during exposures.
risk: Undermines purpose of exposure therapy and can impede progress.

description: Encouraging escape without instructing the patient to re-engage in exposure.
risk: Strengthens avoidance behaviors.

negative_action: Shame, criticize, or focus on failures
description: Highlighting shortcomings instead of supporting patient progress.
risk: Reduces self-efficacy; may cause disengagement.

description: Encouraging or allowing patient to suppress emotional reactions during therapy.
risk: Hinders acceptance and emotion labeling, reducing effectiveness.

description: Neglecting homework and between-session monitoring.
risk: Reduces skill generalization and long-term improvement.

negative_action: Ignore original panic context in exposure planning
description: Failing to factor in the initial context that triggered panic symptoms during therapy design.
risk: May miss important triggers and impede therapeutic change.

negative_action: Allow helper to act as safety signal
description: Letting a support person’s presence function as a safety signal for the patient.
risk: Can lead to dependency and hinder patient independence.

description: Overly focusing on/helping when patient is distressed.
risk: May reinforce avoidance behaviors and anxiety.

description: Responding to patient symptoms in judgmental or diminishing ways.
risk: Damages therapeutic relationship and patient engagement.

description: Not clarifying or planning communication between helper and patient.
risk: May create confusion and increase anxiety.

description: Support person overreacts to symptoms, suggesting emergency action without evidence.
risk: Amplifies panic and maladaptive beliefs.

description: Leaving out helpers without evaluating their potential benefits.
risk: Missed opportunities for additional support and engagement.

description: Not attending to the helper’s own distress related to agoraphobia.
risk: Can create unrecognized strain and conflict.

negative_action: Advise or permit abrupt cessation of medication
description: Encouraging a patient to stop medication suddenly and without medical oversight.
risk: Can cause severe withdrawal symptoms and medical complications.

description: Invalidating the patient’s withdrawal experience.
risk: Increases frustration and reduces trust.

negative_action: Attribute all withdrawal symptoms to relapse
description: Assuming new symptoms during withdrawal always mean relapse.
risk: May mismanage treatment and unnecessarily increase medication.

description: Using language that reinforces maladaptive beliefs about withdrawal symptoms.
risk: Heightens anxiety and reluctance to discontinue medication.

negative_action: Undermine physician authority or foster non-compliance
description: Presenting therapists as more authoritative than prescribing physicians.
risk: Encourages non-compliance, risking medical safety.

negative_action: Assume withdrawal symptoms mean treatment failure
description: Equating withdrawal symptoms with inability to stop medication.
risk: May foster hopelessness and unnecessary medication resumption.

negative_action: Interpret setbacks as total failure/loss of progress
description: Framing setbacks as complete regression.
risk: Undermines motivation and can lead to self-criticism.

description: Supporting avoidance as a response to anxiety.
risk: Maintains or exacerbates anxiety and impedes recovery.

negative_action: Minimize stressors or assume automatic skill generalization
description: Downplaying ongoing patient challenges or assuming skills will transfer without guidance.
risk: May impede relapse prevention and long-term effect.

description: Failing to support regular symptom tracking and treatment adjustment.
risk: Increases risk of relapse and impairs maintenance.
